pages.text:
Multi-Site Outage Post-Incident Report — INC-3312
Affected Sites: DC-North, DC-South
Executive Summary
A regional fiber cut on 22 July disrupted connectivity between DC-North and DC-South, triggering
cascading effects at both sites due to a shared authentication service that was, contrary to design
intent, only deployed at DC-North without a local fallback at DC-South. This report documents both
sites' timelines, impact, and root cause separately, since the two sites experienced different failure
modes despite sharing a single triggering event.
DC-North Timeline
14:02 — Fiber cut occurs on the regional transport ring due to third-party construction work; automated
alert fires within 90 seconds on transport monitoring.
14:05 — DC-North duty engineer acknowledges the alert and confirms loss of the primary transport
path to DC-South.
14:08 — Automatic failover to the backup microwave transport link begins; DC-North's own services
remain unaffected since authentication is locally hosted.
14:11 — Failover completes; DC-North reports normal operation throughout, aside from the brief
3-minute failover window during which cross-site replication was paused.
14:20 — DC-North engineering confirms no customer-facing impact at their site.
DC-South Timeline
14:02 — Same fiber cut occurs; DC-South's authentication requests, which depend on the
DC-North-hosted authentication service, begin timing out.
14:04 — Customer login failures begin appearing across DC-South-hosted applications; monitoring
shows failure rate climbing from 0% to 40% within two minutes.
14:09 — DC-South on-call escalates to the authentication platform team, who were not initially aware of
the fiber cut since their alerts are scoped to application-layer errors, not transport-layer events.
14:17 — Platform team identifies that DC-South has no local authentication fallback and begins
manually redirecting authentication traffic over the (now-recovered) microwave backup link shared with
DC-North's transport recovery.
14:34 — Authentication traffic successfully rerouted; login failure rate drops to under 2%.
14:41 — Failure rate confirmed at 0%; DC-South incident declared resolved. Total customer-facing
impact window at DC-South: from first failure to resolution.
Impact Summary Table
Site Customer-Facing Impact Peak Failure Rate Root Contributing Factor
DC-North None (internal failover only) 0% N/A — transport redundancy worked as designed
DC-South Login failures 40% No local authentication fallback
Root Cause Analysis

rows: N/A — transport redundancy worked as designed

pages.text:
The triggering event — a third-party fiber cut — was outside the organization's control and is not
considered part of the root cause. The actual root cause is an architectural gap: the authentication
service was designed to be deployed redundantly at both sites, per the original 2023 design document,
but the DC-South deployment was deprioritized during the original rollout and never completed. This
gap had not caused a visible incident before because DC-North and DC-South transport connectivity
had not previously failed since the microwave backup link was commissioned two years ago. The delay
between the fiber cut and traffic rerouting (14:02 to 14:34 at DC-South) was extended by the platform
team's initial lack of awareness of the transport-layer event, since application monitoring and transport
monitoring are currently on separate alerting systems with no cross-linking.
Follow-up Actions
(1) Complete the deferred DC-South local authentication deployment, closing the original 2023 design
gap — assigned to the platform team, 6-week deadline. (2) Cross-link transport-layer alerts to
application-layer on-call rotations so a transport event automatically notifies affected application teams
— assigned to the monitoring team, 3-week deadline. (3) Conduct a full redundancy audit of all shared
services between DC-North and DC-South to identify any other single-site dependencies — assigned
to the architecture team, 8-week deadline.
